rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse opens an appeal to reflection and continues the prior contrast between God and idols.
rows.anchor: هذا ابتداء تنبيه على العبرة والنظر، ويتصل المعنى بما قبله

rows.speaker: مجاهد وأبو مالك
rows.claim: Mujahid and Abu Malik mean the cleft in barley grain and date stone.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد وأبو مالك هذه إشارة إلى الشق الذي في حبة البر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says that reading restricts the lesson to some grains and stones without reason.
rows.anchor: والعبرة على هذا القول مخصوصة في بعض الحب وبعض النوى،

rows.speaker: الضحاك وقتادة والسدي وغيرهما
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk, Qatāda, al-Suddī, and others mean God splits every seed for its plant and kernel for its tree.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك وقتادة والسدي وغيرهما هذه إشارة إلى فعل الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya prefers this comprehensive reading as giving the full lesson.
rows.anchor: وهذا هو الظاهر الذي يعطي العبرة التامة،

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says fāliq means creator.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك: فالق بمعنى خالق،

rows.speaker: السدي وأبو مالك
rows.claim: Al-Suddī and Abu Malik see green plants and trees emerging from dry seeds; greenness is life, dryness death.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي وأبو مالك: يخرج الحي من الميت إشارة إلى إخراج النبات الأخضر

rows.speaker: السدي وأبو مالك
rows.claim: They see dry matter emerging from plants and trees as the dead from the living.
rows.anchor: ومخرج الميت من الحي إشارة إلى إخراج اليابس من النبات والشجر،

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وغيره
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and others mean living humans from lifeless semen and semen from living humans, likewise animals, birds, fish, and creatures from eggs.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس وغيره، بل ذلك كله إشارة إلى إخراج الإنسان الحي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya prefers Ibn ʿAbbās's reading; the interpretations are distinct lessons, while the first relies on matching the seed and kernel phrase.
rows.anchor: وهذا القول أرجح وإنما تعلق قائلو القول الأول بتناسب تأويلهم

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan means believers from unbelievers and unbelievers from believers.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: المعنى يخرج المؤمن من الكافر والكافر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘That is God’ is a subject-predicate construction serving as a warning; fa-annā tuʾfakūn means how are you turned away.
rows.anchor: ذلكم الله ابتداء وخبر متضمن التنبيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fāliq al-iṣbāḥ means splitting and bringing forth dawn; al-falaq is morning.
rows.anchor: وفالق الإصباح أي شاقه ومظهره، والفلق الصبح،

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read al-iṣbāḥ with kasra on hamza.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور «فالق الإصباح» بكسر الهمزة،

rows.speaker: الحسن بن أبي الحسن وعيسى بن عمر وأبو رجاء
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan b. Abi al-Ḥasan, ʿĪsā b. ʿUmar, and Abu Raja read al-aṣbāḥ with fatḥa, plural of ṣubḥ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن بن أبي الحسن وعيسى بن عمر وأبو رجاء «فالق الأصباح» بفتح الهمزة

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: A group drops tanwīn from fāliq to avoid meeting still consonants and makes al-iṣbāḥ its object; Ibn ʿAṭiyya calls this anomalous. Sibawayh allows it in poetry, and al-Naḥḥās reports al-Mubarrad allows it in speech.
rows.anchor: وقرأت فرقة «فالق الإصباح» بحذف التنوين «فالق» لالتقاء الساكنين،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sibawayh cites an anonymous verse as poetic evidence for the construction.
rows.anchor: فألفيته غير مستعتب ... ولا ذاكر الله إلا قليلا

rows.speaker: أبو حيوة وإبراهيم النخعي ويحيى بن وثاب
rows.claim: Abu Ḥaywa, Ibrahim al-Nakhaʿī, and Yaḥyā b. Waththāb read falaq al-iṣbāḥ as a past verb.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو حيوة وإبراهيم النخعي ويحيى بن وثاب «فلق الإصباح» بفعل ماض،

rows.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr, Nāfiʿ, Abu ʿAmr, and Ibn ʿĀmir read wa-jāʿil al-layl; ʿĀṣim, Ḥamza, and al-Kisāʾī read wa-jaʿala.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر «وجاعل الليل»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The past-tense form aligns fāliq with falaq; accusative sun and moon support it.
rows.anchor: وهذا لما كان «فالق» بمعنى الماضي فكأن اللفظ «فلق الإصباح»

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read sakanan; Yaʿqūb is reported to read sākinan, but Abu ʿAmr al-Dānī says the report is unsound.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور «سكنا» وروي عن يعقوب «ساكنا» قال أبو عمرو الداني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With wa-jāʿil, sakanan is accusative through an implied verb because the participle has past force; it means He makes night a rest. Abu ʿAlī says the accusative follows the wording's sense of giving.
rows.anchor: ونصبه بفعل مضمر إذا قرأنا «وجاعل» لأنه بمعنى المضي

rows.speaker: أبو حيوة
rows.claim: Abu Ḥaywa reads sun and moon in the genitive, coordinated with al-layl.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو حيوة «والشمس والقمر» بالخفض عطفا على لفظ «الليل»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥusbān is plural of ḥisāb, like shihbān from shihāb, meaning the bodies run according to calculation, as Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Suddī, Qatāda, and Mujāhid say.
rows.anchor: وحسبانا جمع حساب كشهبان في جمع شهاب، أي تجري بحساب

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid, in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, takes ḥusbān as a turning waterwheel and its axle.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد في صحيح البخاري المراد حسبان كحسبان إلى حي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address includes believers and unbelievers: proof against the latter and a lesson available to the former.
rows.anchor: هذه المخاطبة تعم المؤمنين والكافرين، فالحجة بها على الكافرين قائمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jaʿala means created because it takes one object; it may mean appointed with guidance as an implied second object after li-tahtadū.
rows.anchor: وجعل هنا بمعنى خلق لدخولها على مفعول واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Darkness can mean actual night, since stars appear only at night, or hardships in places where people navigate by the sun.
rows.anchor: وفي ظلمات هي هاهنا على حقيقتها في ظلمة الليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qurʾān names three star uses: adornment, missiles against devils, and guidance.
rows.anchor: وذكر الله تعالى النجوم في ثلاث منافع وهي قوله: ولقد زينا السماء الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other astrological claims are false fabrications against God and unbelief.
rows.anchor: فالواجب أن يعتقد أن ما عدا هذه الوجوه من قول أهل التأثير باطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faṣṣalnā means clarified and divided, āyāt means proofs; people who know recognize the sign while others ignore it.
rows.anchor: وفصلنا معناه بينا وقسمنا والآيات الدلائل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anshaʾa means brought into being; the single soul is Adam.
rows.anchor: والإنشاء فعل الشيء ومن نفس واحدة يريد آدم عليه السلام،

rows.speaker: نافع وابن عامر وعاصم وحمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ, Ibn ʿĀmir, ʿĀṣim, Ḥamza, and al-Kisāʾī read mustaqarr with fatḥa on qāf, as place of settlement.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع وابن عامر وعاصم وحمزة والكسائي «فمستقر» بفتح القاف

rows.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr and Abu ʿAmr read mustaqirr with kasra on qāf as an active participle.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو «فمستقر» بكسر القاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dāl of mustawdaʿ is opened by consensus as a place of deposit or passive participle; mustaqarr cannot be passive because istaqar is intransitive. Hārūn al-Aʿwar transmits Abu ʿAmr with dāl kasra.
rows.anchor: وأجمعوا على فتح الدال من «مستودع» بأن يقدر موضع استيداع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If both mean places, attach them to an implied ‘for you there is a place of settlement and deposit’; if active and passive participles, estimate ‘among you there is one settled and one deposited.’
rows.anchor: فمن قرأ «فمستقر ومستودع» على أنها موضع استقرار

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority place settlement in the womb and deposit in fathers' loins until birth.
rows.anchor: فقال الجمهور مستقر في الرحم ومستودع في ظهور الآباء

rows.speaker: ابن عون
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAwn recounts visiting ill Ibrahim al-Nakhaʿī and learning ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. al-Aswad asked him about the terms; al-Nakhaʿī said womb and loins.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عون: مشيت إلى منزل إبراهيم النخعي وهو مريض

rows.speaker: الحسن بن أبي الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan b. Abi al-Ḥasan says settlement is in graves and deposit in worldly life.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن بن أبي الحسن: مستقر في القبور ومستودع في الدنيا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says earth is the place of settlement and womb the place of deposit.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: المستقر الأرض والمستودع عند الرحم

rows.speaker: ابن جبير
rows.claim: Ibn Jubayr places deposit in the loins and settlement in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن جبير: المستودع في الصلب والمستقر في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People move from father's back to womb, grave, resurrection, and Paradise or Fire, where settlement is absolute; each intermediate stage is settled relative to the former and deposited relative to the next, since deposits entail transfer.
rows.anchor: والذي يقتضيه النظر أن ابن آدم هو مستودع في ظهر أبيه وليس بمستقر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yafqahūn means they understand.
rows.anchor: ويفقهون معناه يفهمون وقد تقدم تفسير مثل هذا آنفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-samāʾ means cloud here; anything overhead that covers you can be called sky.
rows.anchor: السماء في هذا الموضع السحاب، وكل ما أظلك فهو سماء،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Māʾ derives from mawha: wāw is vocalized after fatḥa to make māh, then hāʾ becomes hamza because alif and hāʾ are weak and voiceless.
rows.anchor: وماء أصله موه تحركت الواو وانفتح ما قبلها فجاء ماه

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Some commentators take it as everything that grows; the mention of plants limits the general wording.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض المفسرين أي مما ينبت، وحسن إطلاق العموم

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī includes growing animals, plants, minerals, and other things, nourished and grown by rain.
rows.anchor: وقال الطبري والمراد ب كل شيء ما ينمو من جميع الحيوانات

words: فَأَخْرَجْنَا مِنْهُ خَضِرًۭا نُّخْرِجُ مِنْهُ حَبًّۭا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first minhu pronoun refers to vegetation, the second to the green growth.
rows.anchor: والضمير في منه يعود على النبات، وفي الثاني يعود على الخضر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khaḍiran means fresh or verdant; the Prophet's saying calls the world green and sweet. Khidr denotes freshness, akhḍar color primarily.
rows.anchor: وخضرا بمعنى أخضر، ومنه قوله عليه السلام: «الدنيا خضرة حلوة»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Piled grain includes ears and comparable growths such as pine cones, pomegranates, and other plants.
rows.anchor: وقوله: حبا متراكبا يعم جميع السنابل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘From palms’ expands as ‘We bring out from palms’; qinwān is a subject with predicate advanced, and the clause is object of the verb.
rows.anchor: وقوله تعالى: ومن النخل تقديره ونخرج من النخل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭalʿ is a palm's first growth while enclosed in sheaths.
rows.anchor: والطلع أول ما يخرج من النخلة في أكمامه،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qinwān is plural of qinw, the palm bunch; ʿarjūn is its date-bearing stalk.
rows.anchor: وقنوان جمع قنو وهو العذق بكسر العين

rows.speaker: الأعرج
rows.claim: Al-Aʿraj reads with fatḥa on qāf; Abu al-Fatḥ says it is a collective, since fiʿlān is not a plural pattern.
rows.anchor: قرأ الأعرج «قنوان» بفتح القاف، وقال أبو الفتح ينبغي

rows.speaker: المهدوي والفراء
rows.claim: Al-Mahdawī reports al-Aʿraj with ḍamma on qāf; al-Farrāʾ calls it a dialect of Qays and Hijaz, with kasra more common.
rows.anchor: قال المهدوي وروي عن الأعرج ضم القاف، وكذلك أنه جمع قنو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dual of qinw is qinwān, with inflected nūn.
rows.anchor: وقنو يثنى قنوان منصرفة النون

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والبراء بن عازب والضحاك
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Barāʾ b. ʿĀzib, and al-Ḍaḥḥāk say dāniya means near enough to reach; another view says clusters are near one another.
rows.anchor: ودانية معناه قريبة من المتناول، قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read janāt accusative, coordinated with nabāt; al-Aʿmash, Ibn Abi Layla, and a transmission from Abu Bakr from ʿĀṣim read nominative with an implied ‘for you’; al-Ṭabarī coordinates it with qinwān.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور «وجنات» بنصب جنات عطفا على قوله نبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya calls al-Ṭabarī's coordination of nominative janāt with qinwān weak.
rows.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد: وقوله ضعيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Olives and pomegranates are unanimously accusative, coordinated with ḥabbā.
rows.anchor: والزيتون والرمان بالنصب إجماعا عطفا على قوله: حبا،

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says fruits resemble in color but differ in fruit.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: معناه تتشابه في اللون وتتباين في الثمر

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī allows resemblance in fruit and difference in taste; Ibn ʿAṭiyya adds resemblance in taste and difference in appearance.
rows.anchor: وقال الطبري: جائز أن تتشابه في الثمر وتتباين في الطعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Looking means seeing in a way that leads to reflection in the heart.
rows.anchor: وقوله تعالى: انظروا وهو نظر بصر يترتب عليه فكرة قلب

rows.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو ونافع وابن عامر وعاصم
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr, Abu ʿAmr, Nāfiʿ, Ibn ʿĀmir, and ʿĀṣim read thamar with fatḥa, a plural of thamara; Yaḥyā b. Waththāb and Mujāhid read ḍamma as kinds of wealth, the reading of Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو ونافع وابن عامر وعاصم «إلى ثمره» بفتح الثاء

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu ʿAlī prefers the broken plural of thamara, like khashaba/khashab and akama/akam; the anonymous poem supplies akam. Thamar may also be a plural of plural or be read with ḍamma and still mīm for ease.
rows.anchor: قال أبو علي والأحسن فيه أن يكون جمع ثمره كخشبة وخشب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Poetic akam illustrates akama/akam; analogous weak-final pairs are lāba/lūb, nāqa/nūq, sāḥa/sūḥ. Thamar means fruit or produce; calling the tree thimār is figurative.
rows.anchor: ترى الأكم فيه سجدا للحوافر نظيره في المعتل لابة ولوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most read yanʿ as a verbal noun for ripening; Ibn ʿAbbās explains it as ripeness, supported by al-Ḥajjāj's ‘heads have ripened.’ Yanʿ can also mean standing tall and becoming green; al-Ṭabarī calls it plural of yāniʿ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ جمهور الناس و «ينعه» بفتح الياء وهو مصدر ينع

rows.speaker: ابن محيصن وقتادة والضحاك
rows.claim: Ibn Muḥayṣin, Qatāda, and al-Ḍaḥḥāk read with ḍamma on yāʾ; Ibn Abi ʿAbla and al-Yamānī read yāniʿahu.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن محيصن وقتادة والضحاك «وينعه» بضم الياء

words: إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكُمْ لَءَايَٰتٍۢ لِّقَوْمٍۢ يُؤْمِنُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs call for admonition and remembrance.
rows.anchor: وقوله إن في ذلكم لآيات إيجاب تنبيه وتذكير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison follows believers ordered to leave outward and inward sins and unbelievers led astray by desires.
rows.anchor: تقدم في هذه الآية السالفة ذكر قوم مؤمنين أمروا بترك الإثم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وغيرهما
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, and others take believers after unbelief as dead people God revived.
rows.anchor: هذا معنى قول ابن عباس ومجاهد وغيرهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unbelievers' bewilderment resembles people wandering in darkness with no way out.
rows.anchor: وشبه الكافرين وحيرة جهلهم بقوم في ظلمات يترددون فيها

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read aw-man with fatḥa on wāw: interrogative alif plus conjunction wāw, and man is a relative pronoun.
rows.anchor: وقرأ جمهور الناس «أو من» بفتح الواو فهي ألف استفهام

rows.speaker: طلحة بن مصرف
rows.claim: Ṭalḥa b. Muṣarrif reads afaman with fāʾ, close in meaning to the wāw reading.
rows.anchor: وقرأ طلحة بن مصرف: «أفمن» بالفاء، والمعنى قريب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fāʾ in fa-aḥyaynāhu is conjunctive.
rows.anchor: والفاء في قوله فأحييناه عاطفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The light most plausibly means faith, by which the believer acts and speaks among people; Abu ʿAlī allows the light of Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: ونورا أمكن ما يعنى به الإيمان ويمشي به يراد به جميع التصرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fī al-nās attaches to yamshī but can attach to kāna maytan; kaman mathaluhu equals kaman huwa.
rows.anchor: وفي الناس متعلق ب «يمشي»، ويصح أن يتعلق ب «كان ميتا»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ka may attach to an implied ‘as We revived believers,’ or to kaman mathaluhu, making the compared condition itself adornment.
rows.anchor: والكاف في قوله تعالى: «كذلك زين» متعلقة بمحذوف

rows.speaker: نافع
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ alone reads mayyitan with kasra and doubled yāʾ; others use a still yāʾ. Abu ʿAlī says the forms are equivalent and the deleted yāʾ is the second, from wāw.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع وحده «ميتا» بكسر الياء وشدها

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk identifies the revived believer as ʿUmar; al-Mahdawī reports another view identifying Ḥamza.
rows.anchor: فقال الضحاك: المؤمن الذي كان ميتا فأحيي عمر

rows.speaker: عكرمة والزجاج
rows.claim: ʿIkrima identifies ʿAmmār b. Yāsir; al-Zajjāj says it refers to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وقال عكرمة: عمار بن ياسر، وقال الزجاج: جاء في التفسير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commentators agree the one in darkness is Abu Jahl; the comparison extends to his peers.
rows.anchor: واتفقوا على أن الذي في الظلمات أبو جهل بن هشام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The leading-criminal verse warns that the preceding unbelievers will share the corrupt condition of their predecessors; ʿIkrima says it was revealed about mockers, the intended comparison.
rows.anchor: وهذه الآية تتضمن إنذارا بفساد حال الكفرة المتقدم ذكرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jaʿalnā means made and takes two objects: criminals first and leaders second, underlying ‘made the criminals leaders’; alternatively akābir is first object and fī kulli qarya second. The lām in li-yamkurū is resultative.
rows.anchor: وجعلنا في هذه الآية بمعنى صيرنا، فهي تتعدى إلى مفعولين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Akābir is plural of akbar, like afāḍil of afḍal; akābira is also used, like aḥmar/aḥāmira. Al-Aʿshā's line uses al-aḥāmira for wine, meat, and saffron.
rows.anchor: والأكابر جمع أكبر كما الأفاضل جمع أفضل، ويقال أكابرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Makr is false contrivance or deception; their plotting's harm returns on themselves. They do not know: the word derives from shiʿār, what touches the body; sensory ignorance is emphatic, though denied here for this matter.
rows.anchor: والمكر التخيل بالباطل والخديعة ونحوهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yawm is governed by implied udhkur or possibly the preceding wali, coordinated with the syntactic position of 6:127's ‘because of what they did.’
rows.anchor: يوم نصب بفعل مضمر تقديره واذكر يوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun includes both jinn and human groups, unbelievers under defilement and those granted the Abode of Peace; ‘all together’ confirms the scope.
rows.anchor: والضمير في يحشرهم عائد على الطائفتين الذين يجعل الله الرجس

rows.speaker: حفص عن عاصم
rows.claim: Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim reads with yāʾ, others with nūn; both are valid.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حفص عن عاصم «يحشرهم» بالياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An implied verb before ‘O company of jinn’ is estimated as ‘We say.’ Al-ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, and Qatāda say the jinn excessively misled humans.
rows.anchor: وفي الكلام فعل مضمر يدل عليه ظاهر الكلام تقديره نقول يا معشر الجن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human allies speak in excuse, saying both sides benefited. Al-Ṭabarī recounts Arabs seeking a valley jinn's protection; they credited safety to the jinn. Other worldly forms of benefit are possible.
rows.anchor: وقال الكفار من الإنس وهم أولياء الجن الموبخين على جهة الاعتذار

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī says the appointed term is death; other views say Resurrection or the limit of mutual enjoyment, acknowledging God's decree.
rows.anchor: قال السدي هو الموت الذي انتهى الكل منهم إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's report follows their plea; past tense reports certain future action, common and eloquent Qurʾānic usage.
rows.anchor: وقوله تعالى: قال النار مثواكم الآية، إخبار من الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: الزجاج وأبو علي
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj takes mathwā as place of recompense or abode. Abu ʿAlī takes it as verbal noun because it governs khalidīn, estimating ‘the Fire is the possessor of your abode.’
rows.anchor: ومثواكم أي موضع ثوابكم كمقامكم الذي هو موضع الإقامة،

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: One group takes mā as man, exempting those who believe in worldly life after unbelief.
rows.anchor: قالت فرقة ما بمعنى من، فالمراد إلا من شاء

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says illā means ‘other than’ and the exception is added punishment God wills; al-Zajjāj inclines to this. Al-Ṭabarī takes it as the interval before entry into Fire, which Ibn ʿAṭiyya says the wording permits.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء إلا بمعنى سوى، والمراد سوى ما يشاء من زيادة

rows.speaker: الطبري عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī reports Ibn ʿAbbās said the exception is their final state known to God and no one should judge whether God puts a person in Paradise or Fire; Ibn ʿAṭiyya rejects this as unsound against consensus of eternal punishment.
rows.anchor: وقال الطبري عن ابن عباس انه كان يتناول في هذا الاستثناء أنه مبلغ حال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya prefers the exception as an address to the Prophet and community, exempting unbelievers whom God knows will later believe; mā can denote rational persons, and Wise/Knowing fits this knowledge and just punishment.
rows.anchor: ويتجه عندي في هذا الاستثناء أن يكون مخاطبة للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says God makes wrongdoers allies in unbelief and wrongdoing, or makes them follow one another into Fire. Ibn ʿAṭiyya prefers the former from the prior mention of jinn, humans, and mutual enjoyment.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة نولي معناه نجعل بعضهم ولي بعض في الكفر

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says God gives some wrongdoers power over others as allies in punishment; Ibn ʿAṭiyya says this lacks support from preceding wording but cites Ibn al-Zubayr applying the verse after ʿAbd al-Malik killed ʿAmr b. Saʿīd.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن زيد معناه نسلط بعض الظالمين على بعض

none: Bare transition heading only; no commentary point.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After prohibitions for Muḥammad's community, Jewish prohibitions refute their claim God forbade nothing and Israel chose the restrictions; hādū and Jews were discussed in al-Baqara.
rows.anchor: لما ذكر الله عز وجل ما حرم على أمة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم أعقب ذلك بذكر ما حرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhi ẓufur includes camels, ostriches, geese, and similar animals with unsplit toes and nails. Abu Zayd restricts it to camels, which Ibn ʿAṭiyya rejects; Thaʿlab's predator/non-predator distinction fails because lions have nails.
rows.anchor: وكل ذي ظفر يراد به الإبل والنعام والإوز ونحوه من الحيوان

rows.speaker: الجمهور والحسن والأعرج وأبو السمال قعنب
rows.claim: The majority have ḍamma on both consonants; al-Ḥasan and al-Aʿraj have still fāʾ; Abu al-Sammāl Quʿnub has kasra on ẓāʾ and still fāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ جمهور الناس «ظفر» بضم الظاء والفاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Forbidden fats include caul fat, kidney fat, and pure fat except what the verse exempts.
rows.anchor: وهي الثروب وشحم الكلى وما كان شحما خالصا

rows.speaker: ابن المنذر عن مالك وغيره
rows.claim: Ibn al-Mundhir reports in al-Ishrāf that Mālik and others prohibit fat from Jewish slaughter; this is the apparent Mudawwana ruling.
rows.anchor: فحكى ابن المنذر في الأشراف عن مالك وغيره منع أكل الشحم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the view that ‘food of the People of Scripture’ in 5:5 means meat from their slaughter, what they cannot eat receives no valid slaughter and is like blood in Muslim slaughter; thus a Jew's camel or rabbit is not eaten.
rows.anchor: وطعام الذين أوتوا الكتاب حل لكم بأنه المطعوم من ذبائحهم

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Another report says Mālik merely disliked fat from People of Scripture, not that he prohibited it; some permit such fat and their slaughter of animals forbidden to them when commissioned.
rows.anchor: وروي عن مالك رحمه الله كراهية الشحم من ذبائح أهل الكتاب دون تحريم
